newsitem.title: UK: IRAQI CRUDE NOT YET LOADING AT CEYHAN - TRADE.
newsitem.headline: IRAQI CRUDE NOT YET LOADING AT CEYHAN - TRADE.

text.p: The tanker Arcadia, due to load the first Iraqi crude of the U.N. oil-for-food deal's second phase, was still waiting at the Turkish Mediterranean port of Ceyhan on Tuesday, industry sources said.
The charterer, U.S. firm Bayoil, was waiting for the U.N. to approve its contract with Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO), they said.
"As far as we're aware they have still not received confirmation from the overseers," said a source familiar with operations at the Turkish pipeline outlet at Ceyhan.
Shipping brokers said Bayoil fixed the VLCC Arcadia to load two million barrels of Kirkuk Blend to the U.S. Gulf.
Austrian oil company OMV, meanwhile, has agreed a contract with SOMO to lift one million barrels of Kirkuk later this month, trading sources said.

Shipping brokers said OMV had fixed the Biruinta loading at Ceyhan around August 27, swapping slots with French refiner Elf who replaced the Birch with the Macedonia loading one million barrels around August 23.
